625.content: Feature sign-off on issue candidate, extracted Stakeholders sign off on the delivered feature on the issue, having tested the built artefact rather than a description of it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#S_FeatureSignoff . Fetch & Ingest Missing Subgraphs (.nq.gz) candidate, extracted Fetch missing partition payloads over HTTP (servedRoute) or local files, decompress gzip streams, and ingest quads directly into store. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/named-query-execution.bpmn#A_FetchPartitions . Fetch the root declaration at the pin, and validate it candidate, extracted A sparse, shallow fetch of the substrate's root declaration only. Two questions: does it parse as bootstrap's KnowledgeGraphDeclarationSchema, and does it declare at least one harness? could not fetch is a third answer and is never read as conforms. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Validate . Fetch, and record fixity candidate, extracted Fetch, then record sha256 and byte count. Fixity is REQUIRED for an archival copy: an archive that cannot demonstrate it is unchanged is a copy, and it cannot be re-fetched to check, because the thing it would be re-fetched from is what it exists to survive. The data already exists — every structure.json carries sha256 and bytes, and nothing reads them as fixity. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Fetch . File feedback as beans [todo-manager] candidate, extracted Triaged feedback re-enters the work plan as beans, which is how the next cycle knows what it is for. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_FeedbackBeans . File info, sizes, hashes, timestamps, mimetype candidate, extracted NOT IMPLEMENTED. Tracked as a bean; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Mechanical and cheap; the checksum is what makes a remote asset verifiable. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_TechMeta . File the signed certification [qa-attestations/v1] candidate, extracted The signed certification goes under the declared attestations graph on main (owner ruling D2 (a), D5 default), pointing at the report it certifies. The bean resolves here, once the process has actually finished. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/test-plan-execution.bpmn#A_FileCertification . Filter the corpus, choose the granularity, decompose the question candidate, extracted The paper's Planner. Three outputs, and the middle one is the method's substance: a filtered document subset, the granularity to search at, and the sub-questions. CHOOSING THE GRANULARITY PER QUESTION is the whole point of parsing at several. A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. This checkout cannot yet offer the choice — l1-blocks.ts produces blocks, there is no summary level — so this step SAYS which granularity it searched rather than implying the corpus offered alternatives. Re-entered on every iteration, not only the first: the sub-questions are re-derived from what has been found so far, which is what makes the loop a search rather than a retry. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn#A_Plan . Find members with no CI on their head [pr-checks-present] candidate, extracted GitHub runs no pull_request CI while a PR conflicts, so a member can arrive with nothing on its head (bean u7be item 3). That member is T2's first suspect if the train goes red. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Call_ChecksPresent . Find the footprint candidate, extracted handover notes (beans/notes, title 'handover:'), open PRs and branches by session or time window, in-progress beans, workflow instances, last PR and issue comments. REST, one batched pass. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#A_Footprint . Find the owner's authorisation for THIS merge candidate, extracted Classify what exists into one value: explicit (the owner's own words naming this merge, given against this head), waiver (a valid memory/waivers/ node with gate merge-to-main, in scope and unexpired), instruction-only (a broad instruction about the work, such as "fix all issues until green" or "ship it", which is not an authorisation), none, or unknown (waivers unreadable or malformed). A sibling agent's message is never the owner's consent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_ReadAuthorisation . Fix the PR, report on the PR candidate, extracted Claims the refusal bean, brings main in with merge:main, settles what it refused, pushes. Completed with the outcome fail condition by the steward when the condition fires first. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Fix . Fix the PR, then re-signal ready candidate, extracted On the sibling's own branch: merge main in, fix, push, and re-mark ready (ready: <head sha>). It re-enters the queue as a new placement; the ejection stays on its entry until a later train lands it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Task_SiblingFix . Follow it, and say that you did candidate, extracted A stated step — a harness's own docs/bootstrap/initialization.md. Read it and do what it says. It stays stated in the record: nothing can observe that it was followed, and the record does not pretend otherwise. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_FollowStated . Follow them, at each location candidate, extracted The instructions belong to the harness being installed, not to bootstrap — bootstrap does not know what any Harness above it requires, and does not need to. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_Install . Follow up, narrower candidate, extracted The answer did not settle it: it named a kind rather than an option, or chose two. Ask once more, narrower, naming what the first answer left open. Once: an agent that keeps asking has stopped narrowing. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_FollowUp . Format Universal Result Response Envelope candidate, extracted Serialize query results into NamedQueryResponseSchema envelope: queryId, executionTimeMs, rowCount, bindings (for SELECT), boolean (for ASK), or quads (for CONSTRUCT). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/named-query-execution.bpmn#A_FormatResponse . Frame the decision and check the trigger candidate, extracted One sentence naming the KIND of thing being chosen, not the options — "which cache strategy", never "A or B". Then the trigger: is this irreversible, or would the answer surprise someone? If neither, say so and stop; the calling step decides without this subprocess. Stopping here is a correct outcome, not a skipped step. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/options-analysis.bpmn#A_Frame . Frame the question as PICO [content-author] candidate, extracted Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome. The PICO is what makes the search reproducible and the evidence auditable: without it, 'we looked for evidence' is not a claim anyone can check. WHO guideline development states the question this way before any retrieval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_FramePico .

626.title: G
626.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). A slice whose rows do not match its source fails; it never passes as whole. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Check . Gather and verify the evidence [evidence-retrieval] candidate, extracted Before anything is drafted: the author reads the guidance ALREADY in this content, frames the question as PICO, retrieves candidates across the three evidence classes, and has each candidate's authority resolved against its publisher's own API. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none -- and is skipped there rather than satisfied vacuously. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#CallActivity_Evidence . Give a link, a description, or neither candidate, extracted "Or neither" is a real outcome, not a failure. The ask says what happens if nothing comes, and then that happens — the work proceeds without the resource and says so. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#P_Respond . Grant a dispensation, with its reason candidate, extracted The rule applies and this subject is a stated exception. A kind: "human" entry with result: "pass" overrides the script's fail for that criterion, and ONLY while its field_hash matches the current source — so the dispensation is scoped to the version it was granted against, lapses when the block changes, and never becomes precedent. There is nothing to overturn later; the source moving overturns it. A dispensation with no notes is not a dispensation. It is an override somebody applied to get to green, and nobody can review it afterwards — which is why this step is not relaxable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#A_Dispensation . Grant or revoke a permission candidate, extracted A permission travels with the PARTICIPANT and cross-cuts every lane, so unlike a role it cannot be scoped by the diagram it is used in. Granting one is a standing decision, which is why this lane is person-only and why the log capture on this process is on. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_GrantOrRevoke . Grant, narrow or refuse each candidate, extracted The owner's answer, per permission, in their own words. Quoted verbatim in the record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/secure-agent-permissions.bpmn#Task_OwnerGrants .

627.title: H
627.content: Hand back, with a fail condition candidate, extracted The agent-handoff format (#1884): Roles, Report to (the PR), Done when, Fails if. The fail condition: no started line within 4 h, no push within 24 h, the session gone, or blocked on something it cannot settle. One line to the session; the instructions are in the bean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_HandBack . Hand it back [merge-refusal] candidate, extracted Red CI, a conflict or a blocking review is the PR owner's to fix, not the merger's: merge-refusal.bpmn records the reason on the bean and returns the PR. The merger does not fix the PR to make it pass. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-to-main.bpmn#Call_HandBack . Hand it back [merge-refusal] candidate, extracted merge-refusal.bpmn (PR #1888, bean zacz): a bean under the right epic, a hand-back to the owning session with a fail condition (agent-handoff, #1884), or a dispatch when nobody owns it. R4: the PR returns with its reason. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Call_HandBack . Hand over the live link candidate, extracted Confirmed live. The link is given as a link, and the author is told what is on it. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ReportUrl . Hand the candidates to a decision methodology candidate, extracted The candidate strategies go to options-analysis, which selects the decision methodology by context and applies it. SWOT does not make that selection and does not make the decision. What is handed over includes the ambiguities from A_RecordAmbiguous and the fact that the candidates are UNRANKED. A receiving methodology that assumed an ordered list would be reading a priority SWOT never established. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_HandOff . Hand the culprit back [merge-refusal] candidate, extracted The same hand-back as a refused placement (#1888), carrying the ejection's evidence (R4). Then the train re-runs without it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Call_EjectHandBack . Human / SME review [content-review] candidate, extracted Escalated to a human reviewer or subject-matter expert when the change turns on clinical or scientific judgement. A rendered change reaches the reviewer with its before/after preview (skill before-after-preview). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_SmeReview . Human eyes on the rendered artefact candidate, extracted Bean xies, gate 3, and the one that is easy to drop because gate 2 (merge to main) looks like an approval. It is not: merging approves the CHANGE, and this approves what a reader will actually see. continual-progress measured why a description cannot stand in for it (PR #178, 2026-09-16). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#E_HumanEyes .

628.title: I
628.content: Identify content and target locale candidate, extracted The coordinator selects: - Which content nodes need translation (block, section, chapter, or folio) - The target locale (one of the supportedLocales in <name>.config.json) - The priority and deadline . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_IdentifyContent . Identify entities from the BPA and requirements candidate, extracted Every verb in the BPA whose object is a candidate entity, and every noun in a requirement. An entity with no identifier is an attribute of something else — that test is decisive and belongs to the technique skill. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#A_Entities . Identify the agent Tool(s) acting here candidate, extracted Which coding-agent Tool is running this session, and which others the instance is configured for (each has its own config files: AGENTS.md is read by many; Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and Codex each add their own). The Tool's adapter says where its permissions live and how a rule is written. A Tool with no adapter is reported, and its permissions are left to the person. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/secure-agent-permissions.bpmn#Task_IdentifyTools . Impact analysis what of ours binds it candidate, extracted The half a changelog cannot supply, because upstream does not know what you reached into. Worked from the row's binds list in upstream-pins.json. For the theme: site-chrome/assets/js/docs-ui.js MOVES the theme's own search markup into the action launcher and binds .search, #search-input and .search-label; docs-ui.css overrides .side-bar, .site-header and .main-header; three e2e specs assert the structure the theme emits. An upstream rename of any of those is not a build failure — it is a shipped feature that quietly stops working. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#A_Impact . Import hygiene (HARD) and advisories (WARN-ONLY) candidate, extracted FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE RUNNER — bean 7fu5. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/**/*.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner's ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/**/*.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job's LAST step, where it masks nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-quality-gates.bpmn#Task_Hygiene . Import into the store, and test the import candidate, extracted The part only this process does. Load the landed sample into the chosen store and check what an import can get wrong: every item arrived (count against the request), identifiers survived (the descriptor's authoritative ones), structure validates against the store's schema, and provenance (source, revision, fixity) is attached to each node. A check that could not run is a failure, not a pass. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Task_ImportTest . Import what, where, and who does it candidate, extracted Three questions the scan cannot answer: import these or not; library or content for each group; leave the files where they are or reorganize to declutter. Plus whether to dispatch one ingestion agent or a small swarm. Non-relaxable: nobody's files are moved or imported on inference. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ConfirmImport . Ingest and place each comment candidate, extracted public-comment import / import-narrative: one record per row or cited passage, anchored through review-anchors.json. Status: received. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_Ingest . Ingest into library/ candidate, extracted The harness's basic ingestion flow (document-ingestion.bpmn, Process_Ingestion): the source is accepted, its metadata goes into the KG, and it is catalogued in library/ — held if materialized, recorded as referenced if not. Since placement PR6 (bean apcg) the flow makes no content-type decision: reading a document into sections and blocks — choosing the rung mechanically (embedded outline, pages, OCR), and writing section text only when the licence allows it — is a refinement in the layer above, which calls this same flow first. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/methodology-from-source.bpmn#Call_Ingest . Ingest tagged review comments [folio-review-comments] candidate, extracted Every PR conversation comment that starts with block: <label> becomes a review-comment/1.0.0 todo (open), idempotently, and is published with the preview as review-comments.json. The staging workflow runs this on every push and on every tagged comment; the coordinator owns that it has run before slicing, because the slices are cut around what reviewers have already said. This is the ingest transition of REVIEW_TRANSITIONS. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_IngestComments . Ingest the theme [theme-art-intake] candidate, extracted See ingest-theme.bpmn. The subprocess derives one Theme node with kind sticky|webpage|publication, and refuses a source it cannot complete rather than emitting a partial theme. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_IngestTheme . Inject PO → translated Markdown candidate, extracted Post-processes the completed .po file: 1. Substitutes msgstr for msgid in source markdown 2. Unshields placeholder tokens back to original content 3. Validates structural integrity (paragraph count, heading levels) 4. Validates completeness (flags empty msgstr) 5. Runs linting (doubled punctuation, orphaned placeholders) Tool: translation_inject MCP tool . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_InjectPO . Inject translations (PO → Markdown) candidate, extracted Reads .po file and source .md, substitutes msgstr for msgid, preserves non-translatable elements, writes translated .md to translations/<locale>/block.md. Tool: translation_inject MCP tool or bun run content/pipeline/po-inject.ts . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_PoInject . Instantiate the harness: write its config candidate, extracted Write <harness>.config.json at the repository root, plus the state directories the harness declares, and — where the checkout has a root index.config.json — add the harness to its instances[] (kg:instantiate does both), because the index, not the file, is then what reads as INSTANTIATED (index-config skill); a root config the index does not list fails check:landing-instance. That instantiation is what puts the harness in the navbar's bottom region. check:instance-render must be green on the result; a config that renders nothing is an entry pointing nowhere. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Instantiate . Integrate: call existing processes candidate, extracted The method's steps become a process whose judgement points call the processes that already exist (adjudication, options analysis, review) by calledElement. Nothing is re-implemented. A needed change to an existing process becomes a bean against its owner. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/methodology-from-source.bpmn#A_Integrate . Integration test and QA sweep [content-test] candidate, extracted Corpus-wide checks that a single-block gate cannot make: cross-references, build green, proof status, QA axes across the whole folio. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Test . Inventory the ingested assets candidate, extracted Which graphical assets arrived, for which surfaces of the website or app design, in which locales, and at which VIEWPORTS: every surface at a web width and at a mobile width (owner, 2026-09-23, issue #1023). Read off the ingested artefacts rather than off the intent — a layout the source declares but does not supply is not in the inventory, and a surface the design needs but no asset covers is the one that would ship wrong. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Inventory . Is every derived artefact present? candidate, extracted L1 source to L1 KG is NOT complete while a required derived artefact is missing. This is the gate that makes the derivation steps obligatory rather than aspirational. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_CheckDerived . Iterate on author feedback candidate, extracted Agent receives revision requests from the author and applies changes. Each push triggers a new staging deployment with updated SHA stamp. A revision push does not pass through Task_CommitPush, so for a rendered change the agent refreshes the before/after preview here (skill before-after-preview), and the next review round never reads a stale one. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_Iterate .

629.title: J
629.content: Judge the assets in their design candidate, extracted A person looks at the ingested assets laid out in the design they are for, at BOTH a web and a mobile width. THIS IS A HUMAN STEP INSIDE INGESTION, and that is stated rather than hidden: ingest-theme.bpmn used to refuse to call this process for exactly that reason. The owner's ruling puts theme review at ingestion only, and a ruling that moves a review does not remove the person who performs it — so ingestion of a THEME SOURCE is attended at this step, while ingestion of everything else stays unattended because Gateway_ThemeSource routes it past. A judgement made at one viewport is incomplete, not passed, and the wireframe of the surface (wireframe-design-review) says what each layout was meant to be. Three defects in the landing board — a selector matching nothing, a crop cutting the subject, a fade wrong in both directions — were invisible to a clean build, a passing suite and every gate, and were found only by rendering the page and looking. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#R_Judge .

630.title: K
630.content: Keep it as a trial: the unpublished trashcan candidate, extracted A trial goes to the kept trashcan: addressable, exported, never published. Its node declares $schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1 and carries the bean or issue it was written under, since it was never moved from anywhere and a movedFrom would be invented provenance. It is NOT refreshed: a trial records what the source looked like when it was tried. Promoting a trial means running this process again with permanent = yes, so the gates are asked afresh. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Trial . Keep the local edit, and re-pin so it stops being asked candidate, extracted The local edit wins, so nothing is re-materialized — and the pin moves to the upstream revision that was compared against. Re-pinning is the half that is easy to forget and is the reason this is a step rather than an absence: without it the same upstream change is detected as new on every cycle, and a contributor is asked the same settled question for ever. The record says the copy is deliberately divergent FROM a named revision, which is a different claim from being stale against an unknown one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_KeepLocal .

631.title: L
631.content: L1 completeness gate candidate, extracted See ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn. Skill-backed by l1-document-ingestion (2026-09-30, bean 7bg9; the section moved there from the harness's library-ingestion in placement PR6): its section "What a complete L1 entry holds" names check:l1-complete as the gate and states its three results. Until then this step named paper-relevance-triage, which never existed, and was left uncovered rather than bound to a guess. The gate contains one adjudication (Task_FlagDrift: real, spurious or source-wrong), and its own Task_Verdict records the answer as a reason against the verdict before returning. So both answers reach this step, and nothing here branches on them; Gateway_Complete branches on the gate's completeness verdict instead. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Gate . Land each member [merge-to-main] candidate, extracted Once per member, in train order, at the SHA the train's gate set tested. merge-to-main.bpmn is where merging is a step with its own gate: it reads the head's evidence live (the train's green run is that evidence, and merge:guard re-evaluates it), establishes that the owner authorised THIS merge (explicitly, or by a standing ruling quoted verbatim with its date, e.g. 2026-10-01 "you may merge green PRs", which covers green heads only and only the queue as it stood), records the authorisation, merges pinned to the head, and then confirms main, re-pins downstream mounts and notes the bean. Until 2026-10-09 this was two steps here, Task_Release in the owner's lane bound to interaction-modality and Task_Land bound to prepare-merge; neither could refuse a merge, and neither said what happens when a repository has no CI. R1 still holds: what lands is exactly what CI tested. If main moved after the train's CI started, re-run rather than land. Each member's trainId is cleared, and its preview is then taken down by feature-staging.bpmn. A member the sub-process does not merge (held, refused, handed back) leaves the train with its reason on its queue entry. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Call_MergeToMain . Land it in library/ candidate, extracted A permanent sample joins the library as an L1 source, with the materialization record (purpose, gates, fixity) beside it. From here refresh-materialized governs it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Library . Land the bytes in the copier's own folio/ candidate, extracted Into the copier's own declared folio/, never a scratch area — a directory nobody declared is a directory nobody gates, and the copy would be publishable by accident. The copy is NOT read-only: it is the copier's own content, makes no claim about anybody else's bytes, and freezing it too would mean the next person needs a copy of the copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_Land . Land the feature's PRs [merge-to-main] candidate, extracted Phase 6's "explicit confirmation before merging to main", made a step that can refuse. Once per pull request the feature still has open, after the sign-off is recorded and before the issue is closed: an issue is not closed on a feature that is not on main. merge-to-main.bpmn reads each head's evidence live, establishes that the owner authorised THAT merge (a stakeholder sign-off or the BA's confirmation is acceptance of the feature, not authorisation to merge it, unless the owner's own words say so), records the authorisation, merges, and confirms the base. A PR the owner holds or refuses stays open, and A_Close then waits: the BA's authorisation to close does not cover a feature that did not land. An increment the owner asked to land earlier in Phase 6 went through the same sub-process at that time. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#Call_MergeToMain . Languages: extracted, rendered, and RTL candidate, extracted Every user-facing string reaches the .pot; every declared locale renders without clipping or overflow; right-to-left is laid out rather than mirrored by accident. New UI is where untranslated strings enter, because nothing was stale — there was nothing there before. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Locales . Lay out the options, with what each costs candidate, extracted Every option the agent could narrow the question to, each with what it costs and what it makes hard to undo. Narrow from context first: an option the agent could have ruled out itself wastes the reader's attention. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_LayOutOptions . Leave a reachable way back candidate, extracted Leave the way back reachable: the collapsed window becomes a control in its own position and focus moves to it — left alone, focus lands on <body> and the keyboard position is lost. An action whose inverse is not reachable is not a toggle (bean l4zi). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-open-close.bpmn#A_OfferWayBack . Leave it referenced, record why candidate, extracted A refusal is not a failure of the process — it is the process working. The node stays referenced, which means the graph still knows it exists and where, and the refusing gate's basis is recorded so the next caller does not re-litigate it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_StayRef . Leave it alone (coordinate instead) candidate, extracted Never resolve, scrap or delete a bean another session or a human owns. Claiming is how two sessions avoid picking the same item; closing someone else's is how one of them loses work it had not finished reporting. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/bean-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_LeaveAlone . Leave the content exactly where it is candidate, extracted The reader said no: nothing moves, no position is dropped, and the board is left exactly as it was. Drawn as its own end state because a destructive action whose refusal is not drawn gets performed by accident. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_Cancel . Link L1 nodes into the corpus graph candidate, extracted Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact -- paper, L2, L3 -- resolves to it through library/. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn#Task_Link . Link the work to an issue candidate, extracted Feature work must be linked to a GitHub issue. Scan before creating, and never create one without the BA's permission — an issue is the stakeholder's record, not the agent's scratchpad. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Issue . Link to existing issue candidate, extracted A match was found: ask the person whether the requirements go on #NNN, then link the work there. The issue is where stakeholders sign off, so no phase proceeds without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_LinkIssue . List the harnesses this could be candidate, extracted Zero or more. The candidate everybody has is bootstrap itself. Context may name others: "please set up <owner>/<repo> here" names one, and so does any Harness built on bootstrap that the Requestor mentions. This step narrows; it does not decide. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListHarnesses . List the locations this could install to candidate, extracted Zero or more. Is this a git repository already, or were one or more URLs to repositories supplied? Both are Knowledge Graph Data Stores; the difference is only how they are reached. A location whose root already holds a declaration, <name>.json, is not a blank slate, and says so in the question. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListLocations . List the steps the declarations name candidate, extracted In the order of the table in initialization-steps: declaration, needs, each dependency's instructions, the documents at their IRIs (checked above, and listed first), directories, assets, README, README sections, site. Each step names the declaration that names it, so a reader can see why it is there. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_ListSteps . Nothing is cloned and no API token is needed, so the check runs the same way on a laptop and in CI. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Task_QueryUpstream . Load the active voices candidate, extracted The activated set only, never everything shipped. An id naming no shipped voice is an error rather than a skip — a folio that believes it is applying a voice and is applying nothing has the cleanest-looking output of the three. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_LoadActive . Log a message or an error candidate, extracted Write a message or error entry whenever a later reader would need it. A command run goes in execution (command, exit code, where output went) — never the output itself, and never a secret, token or credential: capture on puts entries in git. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogMessage . Log findings on the bean [todo-manager] candidate, extracted Findings are appended to the bean, so the next agent or human sees what is outstanding. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_LogFindings . Log task-end candidate, extracted Write a task-end entry, with the outcome in the detail. The step is the unit: an entry per step, not one when the whole process finishes, or every intermediate entry is lost. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogEnd . Log task-start candidate, extracted Write a task-start entry before touching anything: summary, actor, and the process/task/bean/branch/session it belongs to where they exist. role, process and task are optional on purpose — do not invent a lane for work done outside a process. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogStart . Log the failure candidate, extracted Every failure path passes through here, so "logged as failed" is a step somebody performs rather than an adjective on an end event. What differs between the ways in is the message, which is an input, not the mechanism. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_LogFailure . Log the start of the install candidate, extracted REQUIRED logging, which is what drawing the call says. Logged before anything is written, so an install interrupted halfway is distinguishable from one never begun. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_LogInstallStart .

632.title: M
632.content: Make sure every step is done candidate, extracted Following a harness's instructions once is not the same as every step being done. complete-initialization walks the steps the declarations name — FIRST the harness's JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, the primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness; then declared directories, assets, the README and its sections, and the site that carries the documents — checks each, does what can be done, asks the person for what only they can do, and reports every step in its state. An agent may be dispatched to run it on its own: it needs nothing but that diagram and the declarations. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_CompleteInitialization . Make sure gh-pages exists and Pages serves it candidate, extracted Provisioning the target, owned by this Tool's subprocess rather than by the general step (owner, 2026-10-01: "need to create gh-pages branch before can turn on"). In order: (1) an orphan gh-pages branch exists — git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages; if absent, push a placeholder (index.html + .nojekyll); (2) Pages is on, Source = the gh-pages branch at / — gh api -X POST repos/<o>/<r>/pages -f source[branch]=gh-pages -f source[path]=/ when gh is signed in, otherwise the exact manual step (Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages, / (root)). Each half is done, not done, or could not be determined; never assumed. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Provision . Make the change candidate, extracted The loop's only open-ended step. Everything around it is procedure; this is the work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Implement . Map values onto the shared palette ROLES candidate, extracted surface / ink / edge / accent, shared across every kind. A palette per kind would be three spellings of "accent colour", free to disagree about what an accent IS. Where the source is SILENT on a role, say so and mark the value a choice rather than dressing an invention as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/ingest-theme.bpmn#Task_MapRoles . Mark incorporated when the change set merges candidate, extracted public-comment incorporate, naming the branch, PR and staging URL; done by the folio's workflow when the PR that closes a change-set issue merges. A PR closed unmerged moves nothing. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_Incorporate . Materialise the part [materialize-remote] candidate, extracted The ONLY way bytes arrive. Purpose first, then the five gates — size, restrictions, copyright, retention, source loss — then fetch with fixity, or stay referenced with the refusing gate's basis recorded. Both ends of that subprocess return here and the walk continues: one part refused is not the subscription refused. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Materialize remote content (the five gates) candidate, extracted The shared subprocess. It resolves the request against the source descriptor, then asks size, restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, and either fetches with fixity or leaves the content referenced. This process does not restate any of that; it waits for the outcome. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Measure the cutover: separation:cutover:check candidate, extracted Run bun run cat separation:cutover:check --site in the SEPARATED repository (Tool separation-cutover-check). Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate and none assumed: every declared layer mounted at its pin; every path a declaration names resolves (check:declaration-resolution — directories, assets, visualisers, needs); no wiring still names the monorepo (livesAt, a submodule, a reusable workflow, a path into the old checkout — lessons 15 and 16); no import or reference against the layer order; and the site builds from the mounts alone. A finding inside a mounted layer is upstream's and is listed, not counted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_CutoverCheck . Measure the signals candidate, extracted Files and bytes per instance, clone cost (bun run cat health), gate time, merge contention, the candidate's cohesion and cut (kg:detangle), wrong-direction edges, and the would-be tools package's import cone. Recorded in the bean; none alone is a trigger. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Measure . Mechanical checks, both viewports candidate, extracted Tool wireframe-check renders every candidate at a web and a mobile viewport. It fails on horizontal overflow at mobile width, on placeholder text, and on a missing viewport, and writes screenshots and a script entry per criterion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#D_Check . Merge each member onto the base [merge-base] candidate, extracted merge-base.bpmn once per member, in order, --no-regen; then ONE bun run cat regen over the result. Tool: merge:train. Always onto the current base, never a cached one (R5). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Call_MergeMembers . Merge main in, regenerate, fix mechanical gates candidate, extracted Merge commits only; never a force-push. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_AgentFix . Merge the base in, without committing candidate, extracted git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main on a clean tree (untracked files refuse too, so the final stage cannot sweep in a scratch file). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge, hold or refuse candidate, extracted The owner's answer to the question Task_Ask asked. Their words are quoted verbatim in the record, so the answer is given in the conversation or on the PR, not inferred from tone. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_OwnerDecides . Merge, on explicit confirmation candidate, extracted The owner says "merge it", and only then is the branch merged. Merge to main triggers: 1. the main site rebuilds with the changes; 2. the staging preview's cleanup runs; 3. the review comments committed on the feature branch land on main, as the review record. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge, pinned to the evaluated head candidate, extracted Through merge:guard <pr> --merge --session <id> where the repository has it; elsewhere with the merge call pinned to the head SHA, so GitHub refuses if the head moved. Merge commit unless the repository or owner says otherwise. Never delete the branch. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_Merge . Mount each instance at its declared path candidate, extracted Sparse checkout of the declaration and the chosen directories, copied to the mount path (by default the instance's home path, so relative imports and sibling discovery hold). Never onto tracked bytes; never onto a directory no lock says this mount made; never over edits to a previous mount — those are left untouched and reported. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_MountInstances . Mount the branch tip at the declared path candidate, extracted A branch source keyed by tip: branch-store mount --id <dir-id> writes the tip's files at the declared path, so every reader finds the directory where it always was; push splices edits back onto the tip, never forcing, and a same-file race is a conflict. The branch's NAME is the declaring directory's storage (or source) — a branch no declaration names is refused rather than guessed. A commit-keyed branch is read per commit through its own store (qa-store), not mounted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountBranchTip . Mount the remote tree at its pin candidate, extracted A remote source (bean 0mpw): another repository's tree at a full 40-character commit. bun run cat mount:remote lays it down at the declared path and locks its tree digest; it is never written back, because the bytes are somebody else's at somebody else's pin. Usually reached through a source.remote instance in the root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts), which expands a whole harness and its closure — Process_MountDependency. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountRemotePin . Move into library/<bib-slug>/ candidate, extracted The folder name IS the bibliography citation key, so a citation and a directory are the same string. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Promote . Move the entry's ref and re-cache the declaration candidate, extracted Only after every held part has been through the refresh. Moving the ref first would make the records of parts not yet refreshed describe a commit the entry no longer names. The cached declaration is replaced so the review that follows shows what the NEW pin offers, including subgraphs that did not exist at the old one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_RePin . Move the pin and open the PR candidate, extracted The pin literal moves in the one file upstream-pins.json declares, and the PR body says what the version range changed in RENDERED output — the evidence, not just the verdict. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#A_ApplyPin . MVP: build the candidate on a staging branch candidate, extracted An MVP is a DEPLOYED BUILD, not a description of one. The pin is moved on a branch and feature-staging.yml publishes it under STAGING/<branch-slug>/, so the reviewer looks at the artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Task_Mvp .

633.title: N
633.content: Name the subject and the level candidate, extracted One sentence naming WHAT is being analysed and at WHICH level — individual, organisational, national, international. The source requires this before anything is listed: "the classification of a variable also depends on the purpose of the practice", and the criteria for assigning a variable to a quadrant "may be more difficult to clarify if the methodology is not used for a company but for a country". It also bounds the known limitation that SWOT "is rarely deployed at lower than the organization level", where one scan drives strategy for units its factors do not hold equally for. Naming the level does not remove that risk; it makes it visible in the record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_FrameSubject . Name the substrate, pin a full commit SHA candidate, extracted owner/repo and a 40-character commit SHA — never a branch, never an abbreviated SHA. The schema refuses anything else (SubscriptionSchema.ref), and this step exists so the refusal is met while choosing rather than at commit time. A tag replaces the SHA only once the substrate publishes releases. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Pin . Name what will move, and where it lands candidate, extracted Before anything moves, name the content that would move — what it is, with its size and age — and where it lands. The confirmation sits in front of the move: an agent never relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_AskConfirm . Narrative description per image, localized candidate, extracted NOT IMPLEMENTED. Tracked as a bean; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Applies equally to an image EXTRACTED FROM A PDF, not only to an uploaded one. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Image . Narrative review candidate, extracted Descend into Process_NarrativeReview. The actor takes on the narrative-reviewer lane for this call path only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Call_NarrativeReview . No CI: run the repo's own gates locally candidate, extracted Only on no-ci. Run the repository's own gates (its tests, typecheck and whatever its README or package.json names) on the merge result, not the branch. Record each command, exit code and the SHA it ran on. This is evidence the owner can weigh. It is not CI, and the question to the owner says so in words. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_LocalGates . Note the bean, summarise on the issue candidate, extracted The merge SHA and the authorisation block on the bean; a round summary on the issue (issue-working). The issue is not closed here: in CRDM, crdm-close closes it after this process returns, on the BA's authorisation. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_Report . Note the main-branch watch [watch] candidate, extracted Second dispatch point: the change was approved and merged, and the root of the site has been rebuilt from main. This is the moment docs-site.yml failed all 30 times over two months (bean xom7) while looking exactly like a green run from inside the repo. note rather than claim, and the difference is not cosmetic. By here the branch-watch bean already exists, and whether the publish SUCCEEDED is a judgement this step cannot make -- the build reports its own exit code, and xom7 is the record of that being believed. AGENTS.md: a bean is not closed on someone else's say-so. So the step records what it observed and leaves the verdict to the watcher. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_WatchMainCI .

634.title: O
634.content: OCR to ocr/page-*.txt candidate, extracted A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently ("Manual" and "Manval", bean turh), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-extract-structure.bpmn#Task_Ocr . Offer the knowledge-graph destinations for the agreed set candidate, extracted THE STEP THAT WAS MISSING. Requirements were elicited, agreed and signed off, and then existed as an issue and a conversation — so the output of the process that exists to produce durable requirements was the one thing the knowledge graph never learned. ONE question for the SET, not one per requirement: a six-phase run can agree many, and asking six times is the same failure as a form that re-asks what it was already told. The options are DERIVED from the graphs this instance declares in <name>.json, read at the time of asking, so an instance that adds a graph gets it in the offer without anybody editing a skill. Never a list typed from memory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_OfferKg . Open a bean for the unverified citation [todo-manager] candidate, extracted An unresolvable citation is not dropped and not silently kept. It becomes a tracked item, so the gap is visible in the work plan rather than surviving as a footnote nobody re-checks. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_RecordUnverified . Open beans for the change requests [todo-manager] candidate, extracted Each requested change becomes a bean, so the editors and agents picking the work up next see exactly what review asked for and what is still open. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_OpenChangeBeans . Open or claim the release bean [todo-manager] candidate, extracted The release itself is a bean: it carries what is in this draft, what is outstanding, and who is holding it. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_OpenReleaseBean . Open or close a role to an actor candidate, extracted The join every other diagram depends on. An empty roles is a DETERMINED empty — it says the actor takes on none — and is not the same as an absent one, which asserts nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AssignRoles . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted Findings: EDIT the one open issue labelled ci-health if there is one, otherwise create it, with the report as the body. One issue edited in place, never a new issue or a comment per run, so the tracking issue never becomes a feed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/ci-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Track . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted Findings: EDIT the one open issue labelled pr-no-checks if there is one, otherwise create it, with the sweep's report as the body. One issue edited in place, never a new issue or a comment per run, so the tracking issue never becomes a feed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/pr-checks-present.bpmn#Task_Track . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted Findings: EDIT the one open issue labelled repo-health if there is one, otherwise create it, with the report as the body. One issue edited in place, never a new issue or a comment per run, so the tracking issue never becomes a feed. The body states that nothing in it has been acted on. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/repository-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Track . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted One issue, edited in place. GitHub's own failure mail is the channel that was already ignored thirty times, so this adds none: an edit does not notify, and a pin that stays behind for two months stays one unread item rather than nine. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Task_TrackIssue . Open the branch-watch bean [watch] candidate, extracted First dispatch point for a CI watcher: the feature branch has changed and a staging build now exists to watch. The watcher is DISPATCHED BY OPENING A BEAN, not by a workflow_dispatch -- per the owner on bean 29ij, this is a task/workflow initiation. That is the whole reason it is an activity rather than a line of prose. A bean makes the watch durable past the session that opened it: the container is reclaimed, and what survives is the claim. Starting the watcher and recording that it is running are ONE declared step, so the two cannot disagree about whether anything is watching. Claim rather than note: the watch is work in progress, and it is idempotent, so re-entering on a subsequent push does not duplicate it. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_WatchBranchCI . Open the rule's citation candidate, extracted Every rule resolves to a real library/ section or a KG node, and carries the quote it was read from. Opening it is what lets a reviewer say WHY the rule applies — and it is the only way to catch a rule that misread its own source. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_OpenCitation . Open the session record candidate, extracted Writes id, actor and startedAt, with open and claimed empty. An empty open is the NORMAL state, not an unfinished one: an agent reading, answering or deciding is in no process at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_OpenSession . Open the tracking issue, naming the failed step candidate, extracted Open the issue with the step that failed, the run link and — for a verification failure — the verifier report. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/publish-alert.bpmn#A_Open . Options analysis accept · revise · discard candidate, extracted On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down. NOT between Gateway_EditorDecision and Task_RecordDecision, which is the pair the work-plan named — in this diagram those run the OTHER WAY ROUND. Flow_21b goes Task_RecordDecision -> Gateway_EditorDecision, so the gateway reads a decision that has already been recorded, and interposing there would analyse options after the choice was made. In the Agent lane, and this diagram makes the reason sharp. Task_RecordDecision is a userTask in Lane_Editor that already names decision-audit, and Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note. Those are two different acts — the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED, the editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN — and putting the analysis in the editor's lane would collapse them, making the same party both analyse and decide. The subprocess's own documentation refuses that: it produces options and a recommendation, and the authorisation belongs to the calling step. CallActivity_Evidence sits in Lane_Editor instead, and that is not an inconsistency: the author performs the evidence retrieval, whereas here the point is that the analyst is not the decider. On the trigger: A_Frame opens the subprocess on opening-brief's trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. A spelling fix that reached Task_ReviewFindings with one mechanical finding exits immediately; a revise-or-discard on a block other content depends on does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis adopt · hold · decline candidate, extracted On the single edge into PM_Decide, and deliberately not earlier: the MVP build and its gates are HOW the options' costs are measured, so an analysis before Task_Mvp would weigh alternatives against no evidence. Everything the decider needs exists by the time the reviewer has finished and the fixable findings are fixed. In the Agent lane, because this step produces the analysis and does not make the decision — PM_Decide is a userTask whose lane admits person only, and putting the analysis in the agent's lane is what keeps that separation legible rather than implied. A subprocess that decided would be a second accepting party. Reached through the loop as well as straight through: SF_UA_8 re-enters at A_Impact, so a run where the reviewer found something fixable arrives here a second time with different evidence. That is a genuine re-analysis and its op="note" appends rather than deduping, which is the behaviour wanted — a second note records that the options were weighed again against changed inputs. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to absorb the impact candidate, extracted On the edge OUT of Task_AssessImpact and before Task_CommitPush, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. NOT between Task_AssessImpact and Task_ReviewImpact, although that is the handoff the work-plan named. Those two tasks are in DIFFERENT LANES with no sequence flow between them — the agent's assessment reaches the committee through Task_CompareBeforeAfter, not directly — so there was no edge there to interpose on. The conceptual handoff is real; the edge was not. In the Agent lane, matching upstream-version-adoption: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and GW_Approved in the Review Committee lane is where a decision is taken. A subprocess in the reviewer's lane would read as the committee analysing its own options, which is a different process. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. Process_OptionsAnalysis opens with A_Frame, whose trigger is opening-brief's — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator does not, and this is the diagram where that distinction has teeth, since Task_EditLogic feeds straight into the assessment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. By Phase 6 the needs, requirements and data model are signed off, which is exactly the evidence an options analysis needs and the reason it belongs here rather than earlier: at Call_Needs there is nothing to weigh, and after A_Implement the choice has been made in code. Note where this is NOT. The work-plan named crdm-requirements-workflow, and A_Implement is not in that diagram — crdm-requirements.bpmn is the orchestrator, seven call activities and a gateway, and Phase 6 lives here in crdm-deliver.bpmn. The call goes where the step is, not where the plan said to look. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. A_Implement carries cat-harness.processes:bean op="claim"; this step carries no bean op, because Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note on the bean the caller claimed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis .

635.title: P
635.content: Package: files plus a manifest of digests candidate, extracted The serialization alone is not a package. A package is an addressable set — the JSON-LD, the assets it references, and a manifest naming every file with its digest and byte count. The manifest is what makes a REMOVED file detectable, which a per-file signature cannot do on its own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Package . Persist the log to the data store candidate, extracted Capture is explicitly on — by <cat-harness.processes:log capture="on"/> on the process or by config — so the entries go to the git data store. Only this branch commits anything. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/activity-log.bpmn#A_PersistLog . Phase 1 Needs candidate, extracted Identify the stakeholders, synthesise a needs statement from the sources, and loop until the BA and the stakeholders both recognise it. The loop is the phase: a needs statement nobody confirmed is an agent's summary, not a requirement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Needs . Phase 1: Identify stakeholders candidate, extracted The agent asks the BA who is affected by this change. The BA knows the domain — the agent does not guess. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#A_Stakeholders . Phase 1: Synthesise needs from sources candidate, extracted From the chat, issue, uploads and library sources, write a clear, jargon-free statement of what is needed and why, tied to a concrete workflow. Post it on the GitHub issue, not in chat, and ask the requester and stakeholders to review it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#A_Synthesise . Phase 2: Map current workflow (BPA) candidate, extracted Business-process analysis here means reading the existing diagrams under processes/ and drawing the gap, so the skill that implements this step is the BPMN one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_MapWorkflow . Phase 4a: Compare the viable options candidate, extracted Phase 4 often ends with a CHOICE rather than a plan, and this is the step that hands it over. Per option: what it does, its pro, its con, what it changes DOWNSTREAM, and how reversible it is — laid out where the rows can be read against each other, then one recommendation and a stated default. A step of its own rather than a line inside A_DefineReqs, because it has a different output and a different reader: the impact analysis is for the record, the comparison is the thing the BA answers from. Folding it in is how it gets skipped — the analysis feels finished, so the options go over as a list of names. When Call_Wireframe ran, its wireframe candidates are among the options: one row per candidate, with a link to its web and mobile screenshots. Skipped legitimately when the analysis yields ONE viable approach. Do not manufacture alternatives to fill a table. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_CompareOptions . Phase 5 Beans + sign-off candidate, extracted The approved requirements become work-plan items, the BA signs off, and the branch is announced on the issue. The announcement is on the single edge into delivery, so the three loops back into implementation do not re-announce. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Signoff . Phase 5: Create beans candidate, extracted The agent mints the implementation beans itself with beans create, running the exact-title existence check first. The engine has no create op — it claims, notes and resolves the instance's OWN bean — so what this step records here is a note that the plan now exists. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_CreateBeans . Phase 6 Implement + acceptance candidate, extracted One phase and not three, because the loops say so: an increment the BA rejects, an MVP that is not ready, and stakeholder findings all route back into implementation. A subprocess has one exit and cannot be re-entered once finished, so splitting this region would have changed what the diagram says. 636.title: Q
636.content: QA working copy, built once (NOT A GATE) candidate, extracted Bean jtfk, issue #2456. bun run qa:working-copy (bean 72a8) — the bootstrap kg-export, then every declared QA writer — used to run INSIDE each job that reads the QA tree, and qa-publish ran the same writers again: nine builds of one tree from one commit, measured at 2,284 of 4,714 runner-seconds (48 %) on run 37659324493. Now the qa-working-copy job builds it once and uploads everything the build changed as an artifact with a sha256 manifest; each reader downloads it, checks the manifest against the hash this job reported and every restored file against the manifest, and only then judges. An artifact rather than a cache, because a cache key built from less than the real inputs serves stale data; an artifact is per run and exact. It judges nothing, so it is not a gate and does not reach GW_Join; a failed build fails every reader at its first step (they run if: !cancelled()), never a skip. Drawn feeding GW_Readers, the four tasks that wait for it; within them typescript-static and gates-standalone read no QA tree and do not wait, and qa-publish waits for it as well as for Task_RepositoryGates.
